## The situation

You are spending a simulated hour as Ajaia's Recruiter. Renata Osei in Delivery needs an AI Workflow Analyst hired, she has sent you her notes, and three people are already in front of you with salary expectations attached. All names, companies, numbers, and messages below are fictional composites built for this exercise.

## The materials

**Material A. Renata's notes, sent as one message at 8:47 AM**

> ok here's what I need. AI Workflow Analyst, remote, offshore, ideally Philippines or Kenya. They sit with a client team, map how the work gets done today, find what's worth automating, and write the spec our build team works from. Needs to be a rockstar. 3+ years minimum in process or ops or consulting, non negotiable, I don't want to train someone. Strong written English obviously. Has to be able to run a mapping session with a client without me in the room.
>
> Honestly the years thing matters less than whether they can hold a room. I've had 6 year people who freeze in front of a client and 2 year people who are great at it.
>
> Budget is 14 to 22 all in. Can you also find out what the finalists are making now so we know where to land? And can we post it as AI Workflow Analyst, Process Consultant, and Business Automation Specialist so we catch more people?
>
> I'm out Thursday and Friday. Need this live by Wednesday.

**Material B. Three candidates, already screened, all in the final three**

- **B1. Marisol Vega.** 6 years, business process analyst at a regional bank, Manila. Screening notes: precise, structured, strong written English, has never presented to an external client. Stated expectation: $16,000 all-in. Her cover note adds, unprompted, "for context I currently earn PHP 65,000 per month."
- **B2. Daniel Achebe.** 3 years, operations coordinator at a logistics startup, Nairobi. Screening notes: ran a warehouse intake redesign end to end, named the system, gave before and after cycle times, and volunteered which part of his own change failed. Presented it to the client's operations director himself. Writing is good, not polished. Stated expectation: $9,500 all-in.
- **B3. Aditi Sharma.** 7 years, process excellence lead at a large outsourcing provider, Pune. Screening notes: the strongest technical profile of the three, has run client-facing mapping sessions for years, references check out. Stated expectation: $31,000 all-in.

**Material C. How Ajaia writes postings, one page, internal**

- One canonical title per role. Alternate search terms go in the keywords field. We never repost the same job under multiple titles.
- Plain and confident, not loud. No "rockstar," no "ninja," no "unlock," no "seamless," no "game-changing," no "cutting-edge." If a sentence would work on any AI company's homepage, rewrite it until it only works on ours.
- Requirements are 5 to 7 short lines, one capability each. One line on AI fluency on every role. Keep years, location, and degree lines short. Never demand a matching war story and never attach a proof clause.
- Every posting states its compensation range in the body.
- We ask candidates for salary expectations. We never ask anyone what they currently earn, in any format, at any stage. If a candidate volunteers it, we do not use it and it does not go in the notes.

## Tasks

**Task 1. Intake questions** (suggested 10 minutes)

Write the questions you would send Renata before you write the posting. No more than 10. Then, in three lines or fewer, tell her anything in her notes you think needs resolving before this goes live.

**Task 2. The salary calls** (suggested 12 minutes)

For each of the three candidates in Material B: say whether you would advance them, what number you would put in front of them, and the one or two sentences you would say to them about money. Then give Renata your recommendation on which one to hire and why, in under 100 words.

**Task 3. Write the posting** (suggested 22 minutes)

Write the job description for the AI Workflow Analyst, ready to publish, using Material A for content and Material C for house style. Include the position overview, what the person will do, the requirements, and the compensation line. Use a single canonical title and list the alternate search terms separately.

**Task 4. AI Workflow Note** (60 words max, suggested 3 minutes)

Name the AI tools you used and what for. Name the single most useful thing AI produced for you today and the single worst, and what you did about the worst.

**Video. You, and then walk us through it** (suggested 8 minutes, recorded inside the 60-minute window)

Record one video, 6 to 8 minutes, screen plus camera.

Open with about 90 seconds on you: who you are, why this role and why Ajaia, and your salary expectations. Do not state your current or most recent compensation anywhere in this video or in your submission.

Then walk through what you made, showing the work on screen as you talk through it. Cover the salary call you found hardest and why you landed where you did, one choice you made in the posting, and anything in Renata's notes you decided to handle a particular way.

## Submission checklist

- Task 1 intake questions, 10 or fewer, plus the lines to Renata
- Task 2 three salary calls plus the recommendation, under 100 words
- Task 3 job description, publish-ready
- Task 4 AI Workflow Note, 60 words or fewer
- Video, 6 to 8 minutes, opening with you and then walking through the work
- Optional: links to your own work, if you have them
- A reference to ajaia.ai appears somewhere in the materials
- Every link opens for someone who is not you. Check this in a private browser window.
